investigation.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-09-04T00:57 with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 — was unreachable when POST /api/agents was called during agent provisioning. Because every check shares the same error message and no evidence was collected, the failure is localized to the swarm gateway upstream dependency, not to individual eval logic or the production-api application layer itself.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB endpoint in us-east-2 serving /v1/agents) was unreachable at the time of the eval run. POST /api/agents on the production-api returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning", preventing agent creation from starting. Because agent creation is the prerequisite for all three remote-agents checks, all three failed with zero evidence collected. The failure is scoped to the swarm gateway / ELB layer, not to the eval runner or the production-api application code. No historical run data is available to determine whether this is a regression or a first-time failure.

possibleCauses: Swarm gateway ELB in us-east-2 was down, misconfigured, or had no healthy targets at the time of the eval run — the most strongly supported cause given the explicit 'bad_gateway' error and identical failure across all three sibling checks.
Transient network partition or DNS resolution failure between the production-api and the ELB endpoint in us-east-2, causing the connection attempt to fail fast (~11 s) with a gateway error.
ELB target group had zero healthy instances (e.g., swarm backend service crashed or was redeployed), causing the load balancer to return 502 to all incoming requests.
Misconfigured or expired ELB listener/target-group routing rule that began rejecting /v1/agents requests at the gateway level.

Eval runner credential or network-path issue that prevents it from reaching the ELB — less likely because the error message originates from the production-api layer reporting a backend gateway failure, not a client-side auth or connectivity error.

ELB target group health checks showing all targets healthy at the time of the failure would suggest the issue was upstream of the ELB (e.g., a routing or auth problem) rather than an ELB outage.

investigation.title: published-observability-snapshot eval fail: status.json is stale at 386 minutes, exceeding the 300-minute contract ceiling
investigation.summary: The AURA observability eval for published-observability-snapshot failed because the snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was 386 minutes old at eval time, violating the contract assertion snapshotAgeMinutes max: 300 (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482). This is an isolated eval failure scoped to the snapshot freshness check; all three sibling public-website checks passed, confirming the public web surface itself is reachable.
investigation.rootCause: The published observability snapshot (status.json) was not regenerated within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot was sourced from desktop-nightly-release rather than github-actions, meaning the automated GitHub Actions workflow that normally refreshes the snapshot either did not run, was skipped, or failed to publish an updated file to the GitHub Pages endpoint within the allowed interval. The eval measured a staleness of 386 minutes against a contract ceiling of 300 minutes, a gap of 86 minutes beyond the allowed age. This is an eval-layer finding; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so no user-facing outage can be asserted.

expected-output.contract: assertion { path: 'snapshotAgeMinutes', max: 300 } defined at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482 — this is the earliest violated contract boundary.

source.infra/evals/status/features.json:383: registry config shows staleAfterMinutes=360 for this check, which is looser than the contract's max of 300; the contract is the binding enforcement boundary that failed.

sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all three sibling checks passed, ruling out a broad public-website infrastructure failure and localizing the issue to snapshot publication alone.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:2164-2172: the runner fetches the snapshot via publicJsonUrl(args.publishedSnapshotUrl) and derives snapshotAgeMinutes from the payload — the runner itself executed successfully (latencyMs=135), confirming the snapshot URL was reachable but its content was stale.
possibleCauses: Most likely — The workflow or process responsible for regenerating and publishing status.json (expected to be github-actions based on the contract's accepted source values) did not run or did not complete successfully within the last 300 minutes, leaving the previously desktop-nightly-release-authored snapshot in place beyond its allowed age.

Second — The snapshot was last written by a desktop-nightly-release process rather than the github-actions workflow; if the github-actions publication workflow is the primary refresh mechanism, a gap or failure in that workflow would cause the snapshot to age past the contract ceiling while the desktop-nightly-release copy remains stale.

Third — A configuration mismatch exists between the registry's staleAfterMinutes=360 (infra/evals/status/features.json line 383) and the contract's snapshotAgeMinutes max: 300 (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482); if the workflow is scheduled to refresh at an interval between 300 and 360 minutes, the contract would fail before the registry considers the check stale, producing intermittent eval failures even when the workflow runs normally.
Lower confidence — The GitHub Pages deployment for the snapshot URL may have been delayed or cached, causing the eval to read an older version of status.json even if a newer one was generated.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Provisioning: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Remote Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-runtime, remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) failed at 2026-09-04T00:57Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm gateway ELB endpoint at /v1/agents was unreachable during agent provisioning. Because agent creation is the first step in the remote-agent-runtime probe (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918: createAgent), the gateway failure prevented any evidence from being collected, causing a total contract gap across all five required evidence fields.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting the /v1/agents provisioning endpoint — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer returned HTTP 502 with error code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning" on every POST /api/agents call. Because all three remote-agents checks share this single agent-creation dependency (createAgent is called before any runtime or state steps can proceed), all checks failed with the same error message and produced zero evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure failure localized to the swarm gateway / ELB layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader production outage.

investigations.title: published-observability-snapshot eval fail: status.json is stale at 386 minutes, exceeding the 300-minute contract ceiling
investigations.summary: The AURA observability eval for published-observability-snapshot failed because the snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was 386 minutes old at eval time, violating the contract assertion snapshotAgeMinutes max: 300 (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482). This is an isolated eval failure scoped to the snapshot freshness check; all three sibling public-website checks passed, confirming the public web surface itself is reachable.
investigations.rootCause: The published observability snapshot (status.json) was not regenerated within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot was sourced from desktop-nightly-release rather than github-actions, meaning the automated GitHub Actions workflow that normally refreshes the snapshot either did not run, was skipped, or failed to publish an updated file to the GitHub Pages endpoint within the allowed interval. The eval measured a staleness of 386 minutes against a contract ceiling of 300 minutes, a gap of 86 minutes beyond the allowed age. This is an eval-layer finding; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so no user-facing outage can be asserted.
proof: failed-check.message: 'snapshotAgeMinutes expected <= 300 but got 386' — the single violated assertion that caused the eval to fail.

failed-check.evidence: snapshotAgeMinutes=386, maxAgeMinutes=300, source='desktop-nightly-release' — the snapshot is 86 minutes past the freshness ceiling and was last written by a desktop nightly release, not a github-actions workflow run.
expected-output.contract: assertion { path: 'snapshotAgeMinutes', max: 300 } defined at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482 — this is the earliest violated contract boundary.

source.infra/evals/status/features.json:383: registry config shows staleAfterMinutes=360 for this check, which is looser than the contract's max of 300; the contract is the binding enforcement boundary that failed.

sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all three sibling checks passed, ruling out a broad public-website infrastructure failure and localizing the issue to snapshot publication alone.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:2164-2172: the runner fetches the snapshot via publicJsonUrl(args.publishedSnapshotUrl) and derives snapshotAgeMinutes from the payload — the runner itself executed successfully (latencyMs=135), confirming the snapshot URL was reachable but its content was stale.
possibleCauses: Most likely — The workflow or process responsible for regenerating and publishing status.json (expected to be github-actions based on the contract's accepted source values) did not run or did not complete successfully within the last 300 minutes, leaving the previously desktop-nightly-release-authored snapshot in place beyond its allowed age.

Second — The snapshot was last written by a desktop-nightly-release process rather than the github-actions workflow; if the github-actions publication workflow is the primary refresh mechanism, a gap or failure in that workflow would cause the snapshot to age past the contract ceiling while the desktop-nightly-release copy remains stale.

Third — A configuration mismatch exists between the registry's staleAfterMinutes=360 (infra/evals/status/features.json line 383) and the contract's snapshotAgeMinutes max: 300 (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482); if the workflow is scheduled to refresh at an interval between 300 and 360 minutes, the contract would fail before the registry considers the check stale, producing intermittent eval failures even when the workflow runs normally.
Lower confidence — The GitHub Pages deployment for the snapshot URL may have been delayed or cached, causing the eval to read an older version of status.json even if a newer one was generated.
